summary:
Paraná is a state of Brazil and stands under Brazil's national framework. The national layer, carried by the parent record, supplies the baseline on criminalisation, hate-crime protection, document markers, entry rules and custody placement.

Facility access is contested in Paraná's own territory. In 2021 state representative Mara Lima introduced a bill to prohibit unisex bathrooms statewide and require sex-separated male and female facilities; on 16 November 2021 Curitiba approved a municipal bill of the same kind introduced by councilman Ezequias Barros. On 4 October 2023 the Curitiba City Council approved, by symbolic vote, a protest motion against a Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship resolution recommending that students use school restrooms according to gender identity, to be converted into an official letter to the federal government. The Ministry's Resolution 2/2023 of 19 September 2023 had stated that educational institutions must guarantee use of gender-segregated spaces according to each student's gender identity and expression, but the Ministry clarified it carries no binding effect and no school is obliged to follow it.

Document markers are set by the state judiciary. In 2023 the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná published a provision guaranteeing inclusion of a 'non-binary' option in the Civil Registry gender marker, then revoked it in November 2023, limiting administrative replacement of first name and sex to 'male' and 'female' only. In 2025 the same court authorized a third gender option on documents.

Trans sport participation has been targeted municipally and is under Supreme Federal Court challenge. On 26 April 2024 Londrina enacted a law banning transgender people from competing in sports according to their gender identity, with a R$10,000 fine for non-compliance. On 26 February 2026 the Londrina City Council approved a motion to bar transgender athlete Tiffanny Abreu from the Brazilian Women's Volleyball Cup; the Brazilian Volleyball Confederation filed suit in the Supreme Federal Court the same day and Justice Cármen Lúcia issued a preliminary injunction allowing her to compete. In March 2026 LGBTQ rights organizations filed suit against the Londrina law in the Supreme Federal Court, and on 7 August 2026 rapporteur Justice Cristiano Zanin voted to strike the law down. The law's final status remains unresolved pending the court's decision.

Paraná's courts moved ahead of the national baseline on family recognition. On 26 March 2013 the General Inspector of Justice of Paraná ruled that same-sex marriage and conversion of stable unions to marriage must proceed through normal marriage procedures, and the state authorized same-sex civil marriage in all cartórios statewide under the same procedure and documentation as heterosexual marriage, without requiring judicial authorization for conversion. In 2004 Curitiba recorded the first recognition of a same-sex union in Brazil, granting common-law marriage status to an English-Brazilian couple cohabiting fourteen years. Adoption has been granted repeatedly: on 14 May 2009 the 2nd Court of Childhood, Youth and Adoption gave a Curitiba couple the first gay-couple adoption right in Paraná; on 27 October 2010 Judge Sergio Luiz Kreuz in Cascavel authorized irreversible adoption of an eight-year-old child with cerebral palsy by a gay couple together twelve years; on 16 September 2011 Maringá justice authorized adoption of two children by a lesbian couple.
tangentialFactors:
Paraná's municipal and state authorities have at times moved against the direction of national jurisprudence. Londrina's 2024 sports ban and Curitiba's 2021 unisex-bathroom ban sit alongside the state's earlier, more permissive rulings on marriage and adoption, so a visitor should not read either layer as predicting the other.

The Court of Justice of the State of Paraná reversed itself on non-binary registry markers within two years, publishing the provision in 2023, revoking it in November 2023, then authorizing a third gender option in 2025. Practice in Paraná's civil registries has therefore shifted more than once in a short period.

Curitiba's protest motion against the federal education resolution was symbolic and directed at a Ministry text the Ministry itself said was non-binding, so it does not by itself change what a visitor or student would face in practice.
localsOnly:
Residents of Paraná seeking to change their registered first name or sex through administrative route are limited to 'male' and 'female' entries under the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná's November 2023 revocation of its non-binary provision, notwithstanding the same court's 2025 authorization of a third gender option on documents; the interaction between the two rulings is not resolved in the sources.

Londrina residents face a municipal law, enacted 26 April 2024, banning transgender people from competing in sports according to gender identity and carrying a R$10,000 fine for non-compliance. The law was challenged in the Supreme Federal Court in March 2026 and rapporteur Justice Cristiano Zanin voted on 7 August 2026 to strike it down, but the sources do not record a final judgment.

Unisex bathroom access is restricted by Curitiba's municipal bill approved 16 November 2021, and a statewide prohibition was proposed in the Paraná Legislative Assembly in 2021; the sources do not record whether the state bill passed.

Same-sex couples in Paraná may marry through ordinary cartório procedure statewide without judicial authorization, per the 26 March 2013 ruling of the General Inspector of Justice of Paraná, and Paraná courts have granted adoption to gay and lesbian couples since 2009.
outOfScopeNotes:
The final constitutionality of Londrina's 2024 transgender sports ban is unresolved: a Supreme Federal Court rapporteur voted to strike it down on 7 August 2026, but no final judgment is recorded in the sources.

Whether the 2021 Paraná state bill prohibiting unisex bathrooms was enacted is not stated in the sources; only its introduction is documented.

The relationship between the Court of Justice of the State of Paraná's 2025 authorization of a third gender option and its November 2023 revocation limiting administrative changes to 'male' and 'female' is not reconciled in the sources, and current registry practice cannot be confirmed from them.

No region-specific signal was identified on entry rules, screening, hate-crime enforcement, care access or custody placement in Paraná; the national assessment applies.
